facts.text: UL 4600 is a standard specifying what a complete safety case for an autonomous product must cover through lists of questions and claims to be answered with evidence.
facts.quote: UL 4600 is a standard that tells a developer what a complete safety case for an autonomous product must cover, in the form of long lists of questions and claims to be answered with evidence.

facts.text: Underwriters Laboratories (UL) published UL 4600, titled "Standard for Safety for the Evaluation of Autonomous Products"; its third edition is dated 17 March 2023.
facts.quote: Published by Underwriters Laboratories (UL), UL 4600 "Standard for Safety for the Evaluation of Autonomous Products" is in its third edition, dated 17 March 2023 [Chapter 12].

facts.text: UL 4600 sets no performance numbers and prescribes no tests.
facts.quote: It sets no performance numbers and prescribes no tests.

facts.text: UL 4600 uses a safety-case approach in which the developer states that the product is acceptably safe for its intended use, decomposes that top-level claim into sub-claims, and supports each with arguments and evidence.
facts.quote: the developer states a top-level claim ("this product is acceptably safe for its intended use"), decomposes it into sub-claims, and supports each with arguments and evidence

facts.text: UL 4600's question lists allow an assessor to check that nothing was skipped in the safety case.
facts.quote: the standard's question lists let an assessor check nothing was skipped.

facts.text: The booklet groups UL 4600 with the assurance-case standard ISO/IEC/IEEE 15026-2 and Goal Structuring Notation as structured ways to organize a safety argument.
facts.quote: The booklet groups it with the assurance-case standard ISO/IEC/IEEE 15026-2 and Goal Structuring Notation as structured ways to organize such an argument

facts.text: The booklet uses UL 4600's question lists as one format for presenting a plan to reviewers.
facts.quote: uses its question lists as one format for presenting a plan to reviewers [Chapter 12].

facts.text: UL 4600 was written for autonomous road products.
facts.quote: UL 4600 was written for autonomous road products

facts.text: The research did not verify UL 4600's provisions on simulation acceptance.
facts.quote: appears among standards "not verified in this research" on simulation acceptance

facts.text: UL 4600 is among the artificial intelligence documents whose applicability the research did not check.
facts.quote: is among the artificial intelligence (AI) documents whose applicability was not checked [Chapters 3, 5, 10].

facts.text: Safety cases have both critics and proponents, and the booklet records both positions.
facts.quote: Safety cases have critics as well as proponents, and the booklet records both [Chapter 12].

facts.text: No regulation spells out acceptance for off-road automatic braking.
facts.quote: No regulation spells out acceptance for off-road automatic braking

facts.text: For off-road automatic braking, a structured safety case ties simulation, physical tests and analysis to claims an assessor can judge because no regulation spells out acceptance.
facts.quote: No regulation spells out acceptance for off-road automatic braking, so a structured safety case is the instrument that ties simulation, physical tests and analysis to claims an assessor can judge.

facts.text: The booklet identifies UL 4600 as the most developed published safety-case template for a product with perception and machine learning.
facts.quote: UL 4600 is the most developed published template for such a case on a product with perception and machine learning [Chapters 1, 12].
